static_traits.name: Zhang Yuhang
static_traits.educational_background: Student enrolled at a small community college
static_traits.social_status: The relationship with like-minded friends is affected by one's persistent negative comments
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; has not yet received psychological counseling before; no similar problem history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly cooperative, neutral tone; thinking prone to negative filtering and catastrophic Anticipation; tries rational analysis but easily returns to a negative stance

basic_info.main_problem: Felt extreme disappointment and hopelessness after reading a favorite author's new book, believing he will never write a good book again, triggering persistent negative emotions and distress, and affecting the pleasure of reading.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizes their extreme reaction to the author's new book is affecting mood and overall well-being, so seeks counseling support.

special_situations.event: After reading the favorite author's new book, feels strong disappointment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If this new book is not good, it means the author is already declining, and future books will be bad too
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuously focusing on and emphasizing negative details in the work, negating past strengths to lower the chance of being disappointed again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He will never write a good book again

special_situations.event: Whenever thinking of that author's works or the act of reading
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once a bad reading experience occurs, reading will no longer bring pleasure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces reading, avoids related topics to avoid negative emotions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Reading has been ruined for me

special_situations.event: Recalls one's high expectations and purchasing behavior before reading
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A rational reader 'should' be able to foresee quality and avoid being deceived by 'bad works'
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to prevent being disappointed again by berating oneself and setting stricter standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have seen it earlier

special_situations.event: When reminded of the author's past excellent works or positive aspects
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A bad recent book means past strengths do not matter
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Actively ignores or devalues past positive experiences to maintain a consistent negative judgment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Past good works are not worth mentioning anymore

core_conflict.wish: Longing to maintain stable appreciation and a sense of meaning for beloved things (reading and authors' works)
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being disappointed again, worrying that beloved things losing value will bring emptiness and hopelessness
defense_goal: Lowering the chance of being disappointed again through preemptive disparagement and pessimistic Anticipation, maintaining a sense of psychological control

object_relations.self_representation: A disappointed and cynical critic, a frustrated person who has lost confidence in reading
object_relations.object_representation: The other party (friend/fellow enthusiast) is a listener who will tire of their negative comments; the author is someone who will keep disappointing people

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When friends or the counselor invite balancing views and considering that the author may just be temporarily set back
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understands others' balanced perspective as downplaying their own feelings, worrying that accepting an optimistic view will mean being slapped by reality again
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a calm tone emphasizing logic and evidence, lists examples of 'quality decline', weakening emotional expression, avoiding directly experiencing disappointment.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When someone mentions the author's past strengths or positive evaluations of her new book
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treating this positive feedback as self-comfort or unreliable isolated cases, believing it has no reference value
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Interpret away positive feedback by picking out negative details and counterexamples, using the phrasing 'so this only shows he is declining' to maintain the negative conclusion.

manifestations: After a favorite author's new book disappoints, develops a negative and cynical view of reading as a whole
Past positive reading experiences are devalued or ignored, hard to find the value and meaning of reading
outcomes: Low mood and sense of hopelessness
Significantly declining interest in and satisfaction from reading

manifestations: When discussing with like-minded friends, becomes embarrassed and distant due to negative comments
Hesitant to share one's extreme reactions with friends

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should' phrasing (e.g. 'I should have seen it earlier')
Takes the external standard that 'rational readers must foresee quality' as a requirement for oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Hesitates to discuss one's extreme reactions with friends, worries about being annoying
Overly harsh expectations and judgments of oneself; repeated self-examination

positive_force: Once had a deep passion for reading and positive experiences (early works brought satisfaction and creative appreciation)
Willing to try new perspectives and cognitive restructuring (expressed willingness in counseling)
Has a few like-minded friends as potential support resources
negative_force: Catastrophic prediction (prophesying the author will 'never write a good book')
Mental filtering and negating the positive (only seeing the negative; past good does not count)
Rigid standards in 'should' sentence patterns lead to self-blame
Persistent negative comments in interpersonal interaction increase alienation and embarrassment
Emotional reasoning and global negativity reduce the sense of meaning in reading

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent negative emotions and negative comments arise when thinking of that author or reading
antecedent: Thinking about her work or the reading itself
Discussing related topics with like-minded friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic prediction, mental filtering, 'should' phrasing and other maladaptive cognitions maintain a global negative judgment of the author and reading
target_behavior.function: Relieves disappointment through devaluing and avoidance, gains a subjective sense of control and tries to avoid being set back again
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased work focus, awkward and distant communication with friends, significantly weakened pleasure and relaxation from reading
